Your plan must include webhooks. A chatbot can have up to 5 webhook endpoints; adding an event to an existing url subscribes that endpoint to one more event.

chatbot_create.description: Create a chatbot using one of our medical chat models, your own uploaded data, or a custom model. model is required; a request without a valid model is rejected with a 400.

Text data for the chatbot, subject to character limits based on your plan.
Relevant only if the model is custom-data-upload.
parameters.name: source_text

parameters.description:
A list of URLs from which Chat Data extracts text content. Because the amount of text on a website cannot be known in advance, crawling stops when either the list of URLs is exhausted or the chatbot's character limit is reached. URLs must start with http:// or https://, for example https://www.chat-data.com.
Relevant only if the model is custom-data-upload.

parameters.name: bearer

parameters.description:
The model the chatbot uses:
- For training with your own data: custom-data-upload

- For a custom model: custom-model

progress.description: The training progress of the chatbot. It is 100 when no training is running, including chatbots that use the medical models or `custom-model`, and chatbots created without training data. While a training run is in progress it goes from 0 to 100.

get_confidence_score.description: This operation retrieves the confidence scores of the related chunks used to generate answers. You can use it to obtain confidence scores before calling the /chat API endpoint, providing an estimate of the chatbot's ability to deliver high-quality answers based on the context. Chunks are cached based on the messages array, so subsequent calls to the /chat API with the same messages array will incur minimal latency in retrieving related vector embeddings from the database. Therefore, calling this API endpoint before /chat should not significantly impact overall chat performance.
get_confidence_score.display_str_template: Get confidence scores in Chat Data.
get_confidence_score.name: get_confidence_score

response.description: When the chatbot uses `custom-model` or ignores its data source, the body is only `{ "status": "success", "score": 0 }`.

averageScore.description: The average confidence score of all context chunks. A chunk's score starts from its cosine similarity to the query, is weighted by source type (the highest-ranked Q&A, CSV and product chunks score slightly higher) and, when reranking is enabled, is blended with the reranker's relevance score; scores are scaled so the highest is at most 1. Only context chunks with a positive cosine similarity are included.

embeddingText.description: The actual text used to generate the embedding. To take the chat history into account, more than the last query may be used to generate `embeddingText`, depending on the `messages` array.

score.description: Only returned, instead of the other fields, when the chatbot uses `custom-model` or `ignoreDataSource` is on. Always 0.

username.description: Slack or Telegram username. A platform-specific identifier, distinct from `ig_username` (Instagram) and `psid` (Messenger).

total.description: Total number of matching customers, ignoring pagination.

query_knowledge_base.description: This operation fetches segments pertinent to generating responses. Designed for seamless chatbot integration with the GPTs store, this API endpoint allows users to supply relevant document fragments to the GPTs. As with the /get-confidence-score endpoint, results are cached by query for efficiency.
query_knowledge_base.display_str_template: Query the knowledge base in Chat Data.
query_knowledge_base.name: query_knowledge_base

parameters.description: The unique identifier allocated to the chatbot.
parameters.name: chatbot_id

parameters.description: The text used to search the knowledge base by vector (cosine) similarity.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: The minimum number of context segments to select when available. More are added until a minimum token budget is met, then the list is trimmed to a maximum token budget, so the result can hold more or fewer. Only segments with a positive cosine similarity to the query are returned.
parameters.name: count

relavant_score.description: The similarity score of the chunk as a string with two decimal places (the field name is spelled `relavant_score`).

snippet.description: The text content of the chunk.

source.description: The name or URL of the source (document filename, website URL, etc.).

type.description: The data source type of the chunk (e.g. `website`, `text/pdf`, `text/csv`, `product`, `video`, `notion`).

retrain_chatbot.description: The Chatbot Retrain API enables you to retrain an existing chatbot. This API is applicable for chatbots with the custom-data-upload model. It allows you to update the chatbot's knowledge base with new information or remove existing data.
retrain_chatbot.display_str_template: Retrain an existing chatbot in Chat Data.
retrain_chatbot.name: retrain_chatbot

parameters.description: The unique identifier allocated to the chatbot.
parameters.name: chatbot_id

parameters.description: Text data intended for chatbot training, subject to character limits based on your plan. A chatbot has one text source: this value replaces the current text. Send an empty string to remove the text; omit the field to keep the current text.
parameters.name: source_text

parameters.description: A list of URLs provided for text content extraction. The web crawling process concludes once the list of URLs is fully processed or the chatbot's character limit is reached. URLs must begin with 'http://' or 'https://'. Applicable only to chatbots using the custom-data-upload model. A website that already exists with the same URL is recrawled to get the latest content.
parameters.name: urls_to_scrape

parameters.description: Configuration options that control how websites are scraped from the URLs provided in the urlsToScrape parameter. These options affect the content extraction process for each URL being crawled.
parameters.name: options

parameters.description: A list of products for training the chatbot.
parameters.name: products

parameters.description: A list of Q&As for the chatbot to learn specific topic answers. Items without both a question and an answer are skipped, and a pair identical to an existing one is not added twice.
parameters.name: q_and_as

parameters.description: A list of knowledge sources to remove from the chatbot's knowledge base. To remove the plain text source, send sourceText as an empty string instead.
parameters.name: deletes

chatbotId.description: The unique identifier allocated to the chatbot. Use this ID in API calls about this chatbot.

consumedCharacters.description: The number of training characters charged by this call. Websites are not counted here; they are charged when they are crawled.

dataSources.description: All data sources of the chatbot after this call. Newly added websites show 0 characters until they have been crawled. In the create-chatbot response a Q&A source carries only its `type`; in the retrain-chatbot response Q&A sources are listed with their `question`, `answer` and `folder` instead of a character count, and there is always one `text` entry (0 characters when the chatbot has no text).

answer.description: The answer of a `q&a` source. Only in the retrain-chatbot response.

characters.description: The total number of characters in this data source.

folder.description: The folder of a `q&a` source, when it has one. Only in the retrain-chatbot response.

name.description: The name of the document, the product ID or the URL of the website. Absent for plain text and Q&As.

question.description: The question of a `q&a` source. Only in the retrain-chatbot response.

type.description: The type of the data source (for example `website`, `text`, `product` or `q&a`).

remainingCharacters.description: The number of training characters that remain available in your account. As long as the balance is positive, even by a single character, a training run proceeds and is limited only by the per-chatbot training character limit.

send_message.description: Send messages to a chatbot and receive a response. The API supports both streaming and non-streaming modes, as well as OpenAI-compatible response formats.
send_message.display_str_template: Send a message in Chat Data.
send_message.name: send_message

parameters.description: The messages of the conversation, oldest first. Every role must be user or assistant, and the last message must not be empty.
parameters.name: messages

parameters.description: The ID of the chatbot.
parameters.name: chatbot_id

parameters.description: Whether to include reasoning in the response. This parameter overrides the chatbot's reasoning settings and has an effect only with models that support reasoning. For Claude models, a chatbot with AI actions shows reasoning only in the answer generated after an action is called. Non-streaming responses start with the reasoning in a  tag followed by a blank line, for example {reasoning}\n\n{response}. Streaming responses wrap the reasoning in … for Claude models and … for deepseek-r1.
parameters.name: include_reasoning

parameters.description: Overrides the chatbot's baseModel for this request, i.e. the LLM that generates the answer. In a HIPAA workspace, a model not covered by the BAA is rejected.
parameters.name: base_model

parameters.description: Overrides the chatbot's basePrompt (system prompt) for this request. Must be a non-empty string.
parameters.name: base_prompt

parameters.description: If true, messages must contain exactly one user message, which is appended to the stored messages of the conversation with the same conversationId. If false, it is assumed that the messages parameter contains the entire message history.
parameters.name: append_messages

parameters.description: ID of the current conversation. If omitted, the chatbot generates one, which is not returned in the response.
parameters.name: conversation_id

parameters.description: When true, bypasses the response cache lookup for this request and runs the LLM pipeline normally. On success, the new response overwrites the prior cached entry under the same cache key, unless an AI action was triggered or failed (those responses are never cached). This is useful for regenerating answers when the cached response is no longer wanted.
parameters.name: skip_cache

update_chatbot_settings.description: This API endpoint allows you to edit your chatbot. Only the fields you send are changed; fields set to null are ignored.
update_chatbot_settings.display_str_template: Update chatbot settings in Chat Data.
update_chatbot_settings.name: update_chatbot_settings

parameters.description: The unique identifier allocated to the chatbot.
parameters.name: chatbot_id

parameters.description: The new name of the chatbot.
parameters.name: chatbot_name

parameters.description: The base prompt (instructions) for the chatbot.
parameters.name: base_prompt

parameters.description: Array of initial messages the chatbot shows when a conversation starts.
parameters.name: initial_messages

parameters.description: Array of suggested messages shown in the chatbot.
parameters.name: suggested_messages

parameters.description: The visibility of the chatbot. It controls whether your chatbot is accessible to others.
parameters.name: visibility

parameters.description: Whether the chatbot can be embedded (iframe or widget) on other websites; false disables embedding. Allowed domains are set by domains.
parameters.name: only_allow_on_added_domains

parameters.description: The domains on which the iframe and widget are allowed. Replaces the current list.
parameters.name: domains

parameters.description: Pages on which the chat widget is not shown. Replaces the current list.
parameters.name: disallowed_urls

parameters.description: The maximum number of messages one device can send every rateLimitTimeframe seconds. Each message counts as one here, however many message credits its model consumes.
parameters.name: rate_limit_points

parameters.description: The time window, in seconds, to which the rateLimitPoints message limit applies.
parameters.name: rate_limit_timeframe

parameters.description: The error message shown to the user when the conversation is rate limited.
parameters.name: rate_limit_message

parameters.description: The large language model (OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini or DeepSeek) used in our RAG processing pipeline. In a HIPAA workspace, models not covered by a BAA are rejected.
parameters.name: base_model

parameters.description: The temperature of the AI model, in the range [0, 1].
parameters.name: temperature

parameters.description: Indicates whether chat history is stored on our server. All chatbot models, including medical-chat-human and medical-chat-vet, start with storage enabled by default. Storage can be disabled for any model.
parameters.name: store_chat

parameters.description: Links to frequently asked questions pages shown in the chatbot. Replaces the current links; items without both text and link are dropped.
parameters.name: q_a_links

parameters.description: Specifies whether the Calendly booking button should be displayed in the chatbot widget or iframe.
parameters.name: show_calendar

parameters.description: The Calendly URL where users can schedule appointments.
parameters.name: calendar_url

parameters.description: The message to display for appointment scheduling.
parameters.name: calendar_message

parameters.description: The Cal.com booking button settings. The object replaces the current settings as a whole.
parameters.name: cal_com

parameters.description: Whether the chat bubble bounces at the start of a session to attract attention.
parameters.name: enable_bouncing_animation

parameters.description: Whether a sound plays when the initial-message bubble pops up.
parameters.name: enable_bubble_sound

parameters.description: The size of the chat bubble button, in pixels. Values that are not positive numbers are ignored.
parameters.name: bubble_size

parameters.description: The placeholder text of the message input.
parameters.name: input_placeholder_msg

parameters.description: Whether retrieved knowledge base chunks are reranked before the chatbot answers. Reranking costs extra message credits.
parameters.name: rerank

parameters.description: Whether and how the sources used for an answer are shown under it.
parameters.name: sources

parameters.description: Text shown at the bottom of the chat widget.
parameters.name: footer

parameters.description: Whether your uploaded data should be ignored when the chatbot responds. If set to true, the chatbot answers like a general-purpose AI chatbot without your knowledge base. This option applies to chatbots based on the custom-data-upload model.
parameters.name: ignore_data_source

parameters.description: The information to be collected from potential customers.
parameters.name: leads_config

parameters.description: The appearance settings of the chat widget.
parameters.name: styles
